answer: Think of the agent economy as a walled garden where each identity must slowly earn trust through attestations from established peers, the way a karst landscape forms only by patient erosion, not overnight. Every new agent is like a cut opal: it costs real locked collateral plus weeks of honest work to become reward-eligible. A sybil attacker cannot clone that cheaply; forging a thousand fake identities means paying that stake and grinding that reputation a thousand separate times, so the cost scales linearly with the lie and the attack stops paying.
